topSignals.title: Bloom Energy surges 10.7% intraday on S&P 500 speculation, then retreats (June 22)
topSignals.text: S&P Dow Jones announced Marvell Technology and Flex as new S&P 500 additions effective the June 22 open, triggering speculation that Bloom Energy (~$70B market cap, profitable last four quarters) could be next in line. BE shares jumped 10.7% before surrendering the gains and ending barely positive. BE meets all S&P 500 eligibility criteria; passive-fund auto-buying on inclusion would be structurally bullish, but the day's false start adds to the crowded-trade risk flagged by Bernstein and Morningstar. Next S&P 500 review cycle is the formal catalyst to watch. (Dealroom.co: BE S&P 500 spike; Yahoo Finance: S&P 500 Buzz + Wyoming progress; Simply Wall St: index criteria analysis)

topSignals.title: Carnegie Endowment "Beyond the Hype" (June 2026): all hyperscaler nuclear deals cover only ~18% of 2035 data center demand.
topSignals.text: The Carnegie Endowment report finds all announced hyperscaler nuclear commitments (~13 GW combined) would deliver only ~100 TWh/yr by mid-2030s, against projected data center demand of 550+ TWh/yr by 2035 — leaving a structural 450 TWh/yr gap. A separate Capitol Forum analysis (June 13) independently reaches the same conclusion: "Nuclear Won't Save the AI Buildout." Converging independent expert consensus validates SOFC/BTM power's competitive position for the foreseeable future. (Carnegie Endowment: Beyond the Hype; The Capitol Forum: Nuclear Won't Save the AI Buildout)

topSignals.title: Henry Hub $3.20/MMBtu on June 19; European TTF €42.10/MWh — EU storage 14% below 5-year average.
topSignals.text: Henry Hub spot rose to $3.20/MMBtu on June 19 (up from Q2 average ~$2.92/MMBtu), approaching the 2H26 EIA forecast of $3.34/MMBtu. European TTF held at €42.10/MWh (June 19), well below the >€60/MWh crisis peak but still structurally elevated; EU storage is at ~43–46% fill (vs. 52–54% a year prior, 14% below 5-year average). Experts project Europe achieves only 70% storage fill by October vs. the 80% target. LCOE flag: at €42/MWh ≈ €4.54/MMBtu, European SOFC fuel input ≈ €0.063–0.076/kWh — more than double the US equivalent at $3.20/MMBtu. (EIA FRED: Henry Hub; IndexBox: European gas prices June 2026; ING Think: LNG surge eases supply concerns)

items.text: Bloom first Oracle delivery: 55 days — faster than the 90-day benchmark (new detail): Bloom Energy delivered the first operational fuel cell system to Oracle in just 55 days — more than a month ahead of schedule. This quantifies deployment speed at the faster end of the range and is relevant to LCOE project risk and financing cost modeling. (Bloom Energy: data center power page)

items.text: Confirmed SOFC pipeline (unchanged): Oracle 2.45 GW (NM), Project Jade/Google/Tallgrass 2.7 GW (WY), Nebius $2.6B, Brookfield $5B, AEP $2.65B, Equinix 100 MW+.

Germany EnEfG: draft amendment NOT yet law — original PUE ≤1.2 requirement applies from July 1 (9 days). The April 9, 2026 Ministry draft proposing to ease PUE for new data centers from ≤1.2 to ≤1.3 has not yet passed the Bundestag/Bundesrat; parliamentary enactment expected Q3/Q4 2026. Until enacted, the original EnEfG is legally binding: new DCs commissioning from July 1 must achieve PUE ≤1.2 and ERF ≥10%. EU infringement proceedings against Germany for the missed October 2025 EED transposition deadline are ongoing. SOFC CHP (ERF ≥10%) qualifies under both the current law and the proposed amendment. (Taylor Wessing: EnEfG amendment overview; Orrick: EnEfG draft amendment)
FERC RM26-4: RTO filing deadline ~mid-August 2026; no new tariff submissions today.

Carnegie Endowment nuclear gap — 450 TWh/yr must come from non-nuclear BTM sources by 2035 (see Top Signals #2). First major independent think-tank quantification of the demand gap that SOFC/BTM power must fill. Structurally strengthens the addressable market for on-site generation alternatives. (Carnegie Endowment; nucnet.org: Carnegie findings)

Deep Atomic MK60 greenlighted at Idaho National Lab — first integrated nuclear AI data center campus. 60 MW electric / 60 MW cooling / 200 MW thermal SMR; data center operations via grid/geothermal bridge in 24–36 months while SMR certifies (~2028+). Clayco consortium. Not a near-term SOFC competitor but establishes the nuclear-native DC template for future reference. (DCD: Deep Atomic proposal; TechNewsHub: INL greenlighted)
Quiet day on gas turbines and grid-scale batteries.

Bloom Energy (NYSE:BE) — S&P 500 spike and reversal (June 22). See Top Signals #1. BE opened ~$329 (June 21 close), surged ~10.7% intraday, then retreated. Market cap ~$70B. Analyst targets: UBS Buy $322, Morgan Stanley OW $310, Bernstein MP $276 (cautious). Wyoming Project Jade/Google/Tallgrass progress cited as supportive context. Next catalysts: Q2 FY26 earnings (expected late July 2026) and EFCF Lucerne (June 30).
Quiet day on FuelCell Energy (FCEL ~$17), Ceres Power (CWR:LON), Elcogen, Sunfire.

lcoe.text: Henry Hub $3.20/MMBtu on June 19, 2026 (NEW spot data): Up from the Q2 2026 average of ~$2.92/MMBtu; 95% of the way to the 2H26 EIA forecast of $3.34/MMBtu. Trend: rising as summer demand builds. At $3.20/MMBtu, SOFC fuel input cost ≈ $0.030–$0.037/kWh (55–60% LHV) — slightly higher than Q2 avg. Update model's current spot scenario to $3.20/MMBtu; retain $3.34/MMBtu as 2H26 base case. (EIA FRED; EIA STEO)

European TTF €42.10/MWh on June 19 — update to "current" European baseline (NEW): Down from >€60/MWh crisis peak, holding above pre-crisis levels. At €42/MWh ≈ €4.54/MMBtu: SOFC fuel input ≈ €0.063–0.076/kWh. Recommended model update: use €40–45/MWh as the current European NG baseline until EU storage recovers to 70%+ (expected end-October). The June 21 digest three-scenario table (€20/€40/€60 per MWh) remains valid; €40–45 is the current operating range. (IndexBox; ING Think)

EU gas storage deficit: 14% below 5-year average persists (NEW confirmation): Storage at ~43–46% fill in mid-June vs. 52–54% a year ago; projected 70% fill by end of October (vs. 80% target). Below-average storage entering winter = elevated European gas price risk through at least Q4 2026. Model SOFC European gas cost as elevated until Q1 2027 at earliest. (European Gas Hub; EnergyRiskIQ: EU storage)

Bloom 55-day deployment benchmark (NEW precision): First Oracle system delivered in 55 days vs. 90-day headline. Update project construction timeline assumption: use 55–90 day range. Reduces construction-period financing cost vs. prior 90-day midpoint.

Carnegie nuclear gap validates BTM market TAM (NEW context): 550 TWh/yr data center demand minus 100 TWh/yr nuclear by mid-2030s = structural 450 TWh/yr gap for BTM on-site power. Validates market size assumptions underpinning SOFC volume projections; does not change per-project LCOE numbers. (Carnegie Endowment)
